getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.summary: Pick a workspace, learn what the wiki is, and see how the screen is laid out.

documents.title: Working with documents
documents.summary: Write notes, upload files, and organize them into folders.

pdf-conversion.title: PDF conversion
pdf-conversion.summary: Turn PDFs into Markdown documents you can edit.

wiki-ingest.title: Adding to the wiki
wiki-ingest.summary: The AI reads your documents and organizes them into the wiki. Chat only answers from documents you’ve added to the wiki.

graph.title: Graph
graph.summary: See at a glance how wiki pages and source documents connect.

chat.title: Ask in chat
chat.summary: Get answers grounded in your wiki and check where they came from.

agent-tasks.title: Tasks tab (agent)
agent-tasks.summary: Hand document edits and folder cleanup to the AI agent, and apply only what you approve.

skills.title: Skills
skills.summary: Save repetitive work as rules you can run again.

meetings.title: Meeting notes
meetings.summary: Record a meeting or upload a recording to get meeting notes.

mcp-connection.title: External AI (MCP)
mcp-connection.summary: Connect an external AI such as Codex or Claude Code to work with your Fruition documents and wiki.

notion-import.title: Import from Notion
notion-import.summary: Bring in pages exported from Notion with their folder structure intact.

logs-notifications.title: Logs and notifications
logs-notifications.summary: Review what the AI did and undo it when you need to.

settings.title: Settings
settings.summary: Choose the display language, wiki auto-ingest, and member permissions.

choose-workspace.title: Choose a workspace
choose-workspace.body: When you first sign in, a workspace is ready for you. Click the workspace name in the sidebar to switch to another workspace or create a “New workspace”. Documents, wiki, and chats are kept separately in each workspace.

wiki-basics.title: The wiki and chat answers
wiki-basics.body: The wiki is a set of notes the LLM takes after reading your uploaded documents. Chat answers come from this wiki, so add a document to the wiki before you ask about it. To change what the wiki says, update the original document and add it again, or click “Refresh wiki”.

screen-layout.title: Screen layout
screen-layout.body: Use the rail on the far left to move between “Home”, “Graph”, “Skills”, “Logs”, “Notifications”, and “Settings”. The sidebar next to it holds your document tree, and the open document shows in the middle. The chat panel on the right is where you talk with the AI agent. Drag the edge of the sidebar or chat panel to resize it.

chat-panel-tabs.title: Two tabs in the chat panel
chat-panel-tabs.body: Switch between the “Chat” and “Tasks” tabs at the top of the chat panel. Ask questions about your wiki in “Chat”. When you want the AI agent to edit documents, organize folders, or run skills, use “Tasks”.

write-note.title: Write a new note
write-note.body: Click “Add note” at the bottom of the sidebar and choose “New note” to open a blank note. Type / in the body to insert headings, lists, checklists, tables, code blocks, math, or images. Select text to apply formatting such as bold or italic. Your note saves automatically, and Cmd/Ctrl+S saves it right away.

upload-files.title: Upload files
upload-files.body: Choose “Add note” › “Upload files” to upload Markdown (.md), txt, or PDF files, or drag files onto the sidebar tree. For Markdown with images, select the .md file together with its image files (png, jpg, gif, webp) or upload them as a zip so the images come along. Each file can be up to 5 MB for Markdown or txt, 100 MB for PDF, and 10 MB for images, and you can select several files at once. Your uploads, including items in the trash, can use up to 5 GB per person, and automatic wiki ingest uses credits.

organize-folders.title: Organize with folders
organize-folders.body: Create a folder with “Add note” › “New folder”. Drag an item onto another folder, or right-click it and choose “Move to folder”. Use “Select multiple” to move or delete several items at once.

edit-permissions.title: Set edit permissions
edit-permissions.body: Right-click a document or folder, open “Permissions”, and choose “Inherit from parent”, “Can edit”, or “View only”. With “View only”, only the document owner and OWNERs can edit, and other members see it as read-only. Only OWNERs can change folder permissions, and only the document owner or an OWNER can change document permissions.

delete-restore.title: Delete and restore
delete-restore.body: Documents removed with “Delete” move to the trash and are kept for 30 days. Open “Settings” › “Trash” and click “Restore” to bring one back. Only the document owner or an OWNER can restore.

convert-pdf.title: Convert a PDF to Markdown
convert-pdf.body: Right-click an uploaded PDF and choose “Convert to Markdown”. A notice comes up before converting. It warns that the converted Markdown may differ from the original PDF in content or layout and may be harder to read, so read it before you start.

track-conversion.title: Track the conversion
track-conversion.body: While converting, the item shows “Converting” in the tree, and opening the converted document shows how many pages have been brought in. When it finishes, a “PDF conversion complete” notification appears and you can start editing.

converted-under-source.title: Conversions grouped under the source PDF
converted-under-source.body: In the tree, the converted document is grouped under its source PDF and labeled “Source PDF” or “Converted”. Click an item to open the conversion or the original PDF. If garbled pages were replaced with raw PDF text, they’re listed under “PDF conversion result” at the top of the conversion, so check them against the original.

describe-figures.title: Describe figures in PDFs
describe-figures.body: By default, figures in a PDF come in as images only. Turn on “Have AI describe figures in PDFs” in “Settings” › “Workspace settings” to write the contents of charts and diagrams into the document so AI search and answers can use them.

markdown-auto-ingest.title: Markdown is added as soon as you upload it
markdown-auto-ingest.body: When you upload Markdown or txt files, they’re added to the team wiki right away. Only documents uploaded by members with the “Add to wiki” permission in Members are added automatically. OWNERs can turn it off under “Wiki auto-ingest” in “Workspace settings”.

converted-ingest-prompt.title: PDF conversions ask when you open them
converted-ingest-prompt.body: The first time you open a PDF conversion, a dialog asks “Add this document to the wiki?”. Confirm to add it so chat can use it in answers. If you skip it now, you can add it yourself later. If “Also auto-ingest PDF conversions right after converting” is on, conversions are added as soon as they finish, without asking.

choose-ingest.title: Choose documents to add
choose-ingest.body: Go to “Graph” in the rail and click the “Add to wiki” button that appears there to switch the sidebar into selection mode. Select the Markdown documents to add and click “Add to wiki (count)” at the bottom. Progress is shown, and new pages join the graph when it’s done. An orange dot on the button means there are documents to add. Press Esc to cancel the selection.

wiki-status-labels.title: Wiki status labels
wiki-status-labels.body: Labels next to documents in the tree show their wiki status. “Not in wiki” means it hasn’t been added yet, “Edited” means it changed after being added, and “Failed” means it couldn’t be added. Edits only reach chat answers after you add the document again.

refresh-wiki.title: Refresh the wiki
refresh-wiki.body: Click “Refresh wiki” in the rail on the Graph screen and the AI polishes wiki pages and adds newly found concepts and links to the graph. When a refresh is available after new documents are added, the button shows an orange dot and a “Refresh the wiki?” notification appears. If you don’t like the result, roll that operation back on the “Logs” screen.

graph-nodes.title: Three kinds of nodes
graph-nodes.body: Click “Graph” in the rail to see your wiki as nodes and links. Nodes come in three kinds: uploaded source documents (Raw), information extracted from them (Source), and connected concepts (Concept). Use the filters to show or hide each kind.

graph-explore.title: Explore the graph
graph-explore.body: Drag nodes to move them, and pan or zoom to look around. Double-click a node to open that page in the document area in the middle. Wiki pages also show their connected source documents. If the graph looks out of date, click “Refresh graph”.

ask-question.title: Ask a question
ask-question.body: Type your question in the “Chat” tab of the chat panel and send it. The AI figures out what you’re asking and looks through the wiki before it answers, using only documents added to the wiki as sources. Turn on “Web search” to look on the web as well. You can also pick the answering model from the input box.

answer-sources.title: Check sources and citations
answer-sources.body: Above the answer, you’ll see how many sources were found along with a card for each source document. Click a card to open the original document with the supporting passage highlighted. Citation marks in the answer take you to the same place. Click “Listen” to hear the answer read aloud.

note-evidence-notice.title: Notes that aren’t in the wiki
note-evidence-notice.body: If you haven’t added the note you have open to the wiki yet, a notice says chat can’t find its contents. Click “Add to wiki” in the notice so answers can use that note. If you edited it after adding it, click “Apply changes”.

save-chat.title: Save a chat as a document
save-chat.body: Open “Chat options” at the top of the chat panel, choose “Save chat as document”, and pick the Q&A pairs to keep. They’re saved as a source document. Click “Add to wiki” afterward and later questions can draw on it too. When the topic changes, start a separate conversation with “New chat” in the same menu.

request-task.title: Request a task
request-task.body: Type what you need in the “Tasks” tab and send it. If a document is open, a “Current document” chip is attached, and if you select text in the body, a “Selection: …” chip limits the task to that part. Type @ to attach other documents or / to pick a skill, and press Esc in the input box to stop a running task.

review-edit-proposals.title: Review proposed edits
review-edit-proposals.body: When you ask for changes to the open document, the AI marks each change in the body as a proposal. Click “Accept” or “Reject” on each one, and only accepted proposals are applied. Anything you haven’t decided on yet comes back under “Review again”.

approve-plan.title: Review and approve a plan
approve-plan.body: Requests that organize folders or change several documents arrive first as a plan card marked “Awaiting approval”. Click “Open Preview tab” to check new locations, names, and changes, select the items to apply, then click “Accept and organize”, “Accept and edit”, or “Accept and run”. Click “Reject” if you don’t want it. Only the items you approve are saved.

auto-approval.title: Auto-approval
auto-approval.body: If approving every time gets tedious, turn on “Creating, moving, and renaming folders” or “Editing and creating documents” under “AI agent auto-approval” in “Settings” › “AI settings”. Plans with AI review warnings or documents you can’t edit still need your approval. Roll back auto-applied edits on the “Logs” screen. New documents you don’t want can go to the trash.

browse-skills.title: Browse skills
browse-skills.body: Click “Skills” in the rail to see the skills you can use. Switch between the “All skills”, “Team skills”, and “Personal skills” tabs. Each skill shows its command, description, scope, and status.

create-skill.title: Create a skill
create-skill.body: Click “Create skill” and fill in the skill type (Document, Folder organization, or Template), command, description, and rules. Click “Write with AI” and AI polishes your rules using any reference documents. The skill goes through a safety review before it’s saved. With “Personal” scope you can use it in every workspace, and with “Team” it’s used in the current workspace.

run-skill.title: Run a skill
run-skill.body: Type / in the “Tasks” tab to pick a skill, or click “Run” on the Skills screen and choose the document or folder to run it on. Document skills are saved after you check a preview. Folder organization skills save only the items you approve.

save-request-as-skill.title: Save a request as a skill
save-request-as-skill.body: In the “Tasks” tab, click “Save this request as a skill” on a request you want to reuse. The skill form is filled in from your request, so adjust what you need and save it.

record-meeting.title: Record a meeting
record-meeting.body: Click the microphone button in the chat panel’s input box and choose “Record a meeting”. While recording, speech is transcribed into the “Transcript”. Click the same button again to stop. “Voice input” in the same menu types up to 60 seconds of speech into the input box.

upload-recording.title: Upload a recording
upload-recording.body: If you already have a recording, choose “Upload a recording” from the microphone menu. You can upload MP3, M4A, WAV, or WebM files up to 500MB. Long recordings can take a few minutes to transcribe.

create-meeting-notes.title: Create and save meeting notes
create-meeting-notes.body: When the recording is done, click “Create meeting notes” to get notes written by AI. Use “Save as new document” to create a document, or “Add to end of document” to append them to the open document. Click “Regenerate” if you want another version.

past-meetings.title: Revisit past meetings
past-meetings.body: Open “Past meetings” from the microphone menu to reopen earlier meetings and check their transcripts and notes. If the recording was kept, click “Listen to recording” to hear it. Deleting a meeting keeps any notes you saved as documents.

export-from-notion.title: Export from Notion
export-from-notion.body: In Notion, export the pages you want in “Markdown & CSV” format to get a zip file. Upload this zip with “Import from Notion”, not with “Upload files”.

preview-import.title: Preview and start the import
preview-import.body: Choose “Add note” › “Import from Notion” and select the zip to see how many folders, documents, tables (databases), images, and PDFs it contains. Click “Start import” to begin. Pages with subpages become a document plus a folder of the same name, and databases become a table document with one document per row. Notion links are reconnected to documents in the app.

import-limits.title: Limits to know before importing
import-limits.body: A zip can hold up to 2 GB when unpacked and up to 10,000 items. Documents and tables over 5 MB, PDFs over 100 MB, and images over 10 MB are skipped and listed separately on the preview screen. Imported files count toward your 5 GB of storage, and PDF conversion and wiki ingest use credits.

after-import.title: Convert and add after importing
after-import.body: Imported documents aren’t added to the wiki right away. When the import finishes, you can choose whether to convert PDFs to Markdown and whether to add documents to the wiki. Click “Do it later” to put it off and convert or add them yourself.

view-logs.title: View operation logs
view-logs.body: “Logs” in the rail collects the AI operations run in this workspace. Filter with the “AI edits”, “Wiki ingest”, “Wiki refresh”, and “Rollback” tabs. Select an operation to see what changed in documents and wiki pages.

rollback-operation.title: Undo an operation
rollback-operation.body: Select the operation you want to undo and click “Rollback”. A confirmation dialog shows what will be affected. Rolling back a document edit also removes changes saved after that operation, so read the notice carefully. Undoing operations run by other members requires the “Undo actions” permission.

check-notifications.title: Check notifications
check-notifications.body: Under “Notifications” in the rail, view “Workspace” notifications (such as new members joining) and “Tasks” notifications (ingest, refresh, and rollback results) separately. Click “View details in logs” to open the record for that operation. When you’re done, “Mark all as read” clears them at once. Turn the notification cards in the bottom-right corner on or off by type in “Settings” › “Notifications”.

change-language.title: Change the display language
change-language.body: In “Settings” › “Display”, pick Korean or “English” under “Language” and the screen switches without reloading. When you’re signed in, the choice is saved to your account so other devices use the same language. The same screen also lets you change the theme, document font, and animation.

auto-ingest-switches.title: Wiki auto-ingest switches
auto-ingest-switches.body: Under “Wiki auto-ingest” in “Settings” › “Workspace settings”, turn “Auto-ingest Markdown uploads into the wiki” and “Also auto-ingest PDF conversions right after converting” on or off. Adding documents to the wiki incurs LLM costs, and only workspace OWNERs can change these switches.

manage-members.title: Manage members and permissions
manage-members.body: In “Settings” › “Members”, click “Invite members” and enter an email and role to send an invitation. For each member, you can turn the “Add to wiki”, “Refresh wiki”, “Write skills”, “Undo actions”, and “Convert PDFs” permissions on or off. OWNERs have every permission.

mcp-external-ai-role.title: What the external AI does
mcp-external-ai-role.body: Once connected, the external AI does the work Fruition's AI used to do (answers, edit proposals, wiki updates, meeting notes). Fruition's existing rules such as read permissions and saving stay the same. Results from the external AI are not saved directly; they wait for your approval. Because your own AI (LLM) does the thinking, you can keep reading, searching, and proposing edits even after your Fruition credits run out; only wiki ingest and cleanup carry a small separate Fruition fee.

mcp-add-server.title: Add the MCP server
mcp-add-server.body: Add the Fruition MCP server address to your AI tool (Codex or Claude Code). There is one address; you pick the workspace on the sign-in page in the next step.

mcp-login-consent.title: Sign in and consent
mcp-login-consent.body: On first connection a Fruition sign-in page opens in your browser. Sign in as usual, then review the workspace and permissions (read, propose changes, wiki updates) and consent. If the connection request fails to load, check that you are signed in to Fruition and select “Restart request”. An unregistered client needs administrator approval; reinstalling the AI tool may change its client ID, so ask the administrator to check the current ID.

mcp-check-tools.title: Check the connection
mcp-check-tools.body: In your AI tool's /mcp view, check the fruition connection and tool list; this command does not run a search. After connecting, enter a read-only request in the conversation, such as “Search the Fruition wiki for onboarding procedures and cite your sources; do not change any documents or wiki pages”. When the external AI proposes a change you get an approval link; it is saved only after you review the content and maximum cost on the web approval page. Successful document or wiki changes incur the existing MCP fee shown there (saving a Skill is free); the external AI's own usage is billed by that AI service.

mcp-manage-connection.title: Manage or disconnect
mcp-manage-connection.body: In Settings → MCP connections you can see connected AI tools and the work they created. Disconnect ones you no longer use there.
